answer: Proof-of-space-time resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to seal a unique, incompressible dataset to its public key and pass tight Merkle audits along a trellis of challenge windows. Crossing the verification canyon from burst compute to persistent state stops clones from multiplying like an unchecked vine, forcing an attacker to pay ongoing physical storage and IOPS costs per identity. However, bulk datacenter storage still gives well-funded adversaries an economy-of-scale advantage.
